newsitem.title: USA: Rains flood Arkansas soybean acreage, slow harvest.
newsitem.headline: Rains flood Arkansas soybean acreage, slow harvest.

text.p: Excessive rainfall continued to delay fieldwork, and several thousand acres were flooded in Arkansas during the week ended Sunday, according to the latest crop report from the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
Four days were suitable for fieldwork.
Soybeans were 68 percent harvested versus 90 a year ago and the five-year average of 77 percent.
Cotton was 91 percent harvested versus 95 percent a year ago and the 89 average. The crop was rated 56 percent good to excellent, 32 fair, 10 poor and two percent very poor.
Cotton harvest and ginning progressed in several counties. The Dumas Cotton Classing Office reported 507,866 bales classed as of Nov. 7..
Winter wheat was 46 percent emerged and 59 planted versus 60 and 82, respectively, a year ago and the 60 and 72 five-year averages.
Sorghum was 100 percent harvested versus 100 a year ago and the 99 percent five-year average.
Oats were 90 percent planted versus 57 a year ago and the 75 average.
Soil moisture was rated 57 percent surplus, 43 percent adequate.
